memory_candidates.content: git add with multiple pathspecs fails atomically (exit 128, 'did not match any files') and stages NOTHING at all -- not even paths that do exist -- if any single pathspec doesn't match a file. Verified with: git add exists.txt nonexistent.txt. Relevant whenever a command-level git add lists a file that an earlier cleanup step may already have deleted: the failure silently drops every other path in the same call, not just the missing one.

When a shared skill-internal postflight cleanup function (e.g. skill_cleanup) deletes a marker/metadata file before returning control to a calling command, any command-level stage that reads the SAME file after DELEGATE returns is structurally unreachable -- not just the immediately-obvious next consumer (e.g. a defensive-correction script), but ALSO any later command-level git-commit stage that adds/reads that file. Auditing 'who deletes this file' in isolation misses this; the correct audit is 'trace every reader of this file across the WHOLE command sequence, not just the first one after the skill returns'.
